Stem model calculations

Source: vignettes/stem-model-overview.Rmd
stem-model-overview.Rmd

Scalar height, diameter, volume, and biomass helpers return results aligned with their input vectors. stem_profile() expands trees into rows sorted by identifier and height. Only length-one inputs recycle. Other nonempty lengths must match.

Heights 

## Fit the retained inventory heights
fit <- fit_height(dbh = example_trees_pnw$dbh,
                  ht = example_trees_pnw$ht_observed,
                  spcd = example_trees_pnw$spcd)
## Complete missing heights with the fitted model
completed <- example_trees_pnw %>%
  mutate(ht = complete_heights(dbh = dbh,
                               ht = ht_observed,
                               spcd = spcd,
                               fit = fit))
tree ht_observed ht
1 141.8 141.800
2 NA 70.175
3 NA 81.327

Stem quantities

dib() calculates inside-bark diameter. height_at_dib() returns the highest matching height. stem_volume() evaluates a bounded interval using the model’s volume capability.

## Add diameter, height, and volume calculations
dimensions <- example_trees %>%
  transmute(tree,
            diameter = dib(dbh = dbh, ht = ht, h = 20, model = model),
            height = height_at_dib(dbh = dbh, ht = ht, dib = 6, model = model),
            cubic = stem_volume(dbh = dbh, ht = ht, model = model))
tree diameter height cubic
1 8.560 34.120 16.786
2 11.002 44.117 28.156
3 12.195 55.598 39.208
4 14.743 64.505 59.498
5 15.638 76.723 75.958
6 20.140 94.939 136.790

Imperial diameters, heights, and volumes use inches, feet, and cubic feet. Metric calls require centimeters and meters and return cubic meters. Outside-bark calculations require a model capability or an explicit constant bark ratio.

Weight 

## Convert the modeled volumes to green wood and bark weight
weight <- green_weight(volume = dimensions$cubic,
                       spcd = example_trees$spcd,
                       status = TRUE)
value status
788.882 0
1434.825 0
1842.669 0
3031.964 0
3569.866 0
6970.729 0

Green weight uses species properties and supplied cubic volume. The national biomass equations use tree dimensions and ecological divisions to calculate fitted component masses. biomass() returns dry mass, green mass, and carbon by component.

status = TRUE pairs quantities with diagnoses. Unsupported quantities remain missing. Model checks verify available operations and species scope, not predictive accuracy.
